sources.title: UNTP DCC JSON Schema v0.7.0 (ConformityCredential.json and ConformityAttestation.json)
sources.identifier: https://untp.unece.org/artefacts/schema/v0.7.0/dcc/ConformityCredential.json (schema has no $id and no title; identifier is the fetched URL)
sources.legal_or_spec_status: Machine-readable artefact of the pre-1.0 0.7.0 release (pilots). v0.8.0 schemas exist in 'Work in Progress' and are not compatible with v0.7.0 per the maintainers' tracker.
sources.license_or_reuse_terms: No licence statement inside the schema. See untp-dcc-0-7-0 for the unresolved licence picture (CC BY 4.0 footer vs GPL-3.0+ repository vs UNECE general terms).
sources.permitted_use_basis: Read and validate against it by URL; do not copy into this repository until the licence is resolved. Facts about which properties it requires are factual observations that can be recorded in project notes.

evidence.what_it_shows: 27 'required' arrays enumerated (read twice via the fetch tool with identical results). Root required: @context, id, issuer, validFrom, name, credentialSubject. type, validUntil, credentialStatus, renderMethod, issuingSoftware are optional. @context prefixItems fix the first two entries to https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2 and https://vocabulary.uncefact.org/untp/0.7.0/context/. If present, type must contain DigitalConformityCredential and VerifiableCredential. Root additionalProperties true.

Standalone subject schema; required: id, name, assessorLevel, assessmentLevel, attestationType, issuedToParty, referenceScheme; ConformityAssessment required: id, name, assessmentCriteria, assessmentDate, assessedPerformance, conformityTopic
Prose requirements CC-01, CC-03, CC-05, CC-06, CC-07 used for the cross-check

sources.brief_claim_check: matches: the brief asked which DCC properties the specification itself marks as mandatory; answer is the schema 'required' arrays below, recorded from https://untp.unece.org/artefacts/schema/v0.7.0/dcc/ConformityCredential.json. Mandatory per schema: credential (root): @context, id, issuer, validFrom, name, credentialSubject. issuer (CredentialIssuer): id, name. credentialSubject (ConformityAttestation): id, name, assessorLevel, assessmentLevel, attestationType, issuedToParty{id,name}, referenceScheme{id,name}. ConformityAssessment (inside conformityAssessment): id, name, assessmentCriteria (items: id, name), assessmentDate, assessedPerformance, conformityTopic (items: id, name). Conditionally required when the parent object is present: credentialStatus (BitstringStatusListEntry): type, statusPurpose, statusListIndex, statusListCredential; issuingSoftware: id, name, version, vendor{id,name}; referenceProfile: id, name; authorisation items (Endorsement): name, issuingAuthority{id,name}; Image: name, imageData, mediaType; Link: linkURL, linkName; Score: code; Measure: value, unit; Performance: if measure is present then metric is required (dependentRequired), metric{id,name}; ProductVerification: product{id,name}; FacilityVerification: facility{id,name}; assessedOrganisation{id,name}; referenceStandard and referenceRegulation items: id, name.
uncertainties: SCHEMA vs PROSE: the page's prose CC-05 says the assessment MUST state conformant or not, but 'conformance' (boolean) is a property of ConformityAssessment that is NOT in its required array. A schema-only validator will accept an assessment without it.
SCHEMA vs PROSE: prose CC-06 says assessedPerformance SHOULD be present, but the schema lists assessedPerformance as required.

SCHEMA vs PROSE: the page's prose places conformityTopic under assessment criteria, while the schema requires conformityTopic at ConformityAssessment level (and not inside the assessmentCriteria item required list of id, name).

The top-level 'type' property is not in the root required array, so the DigitalConformityCredential/VerifiableCredential constraint only applies if type is present. The credential subject's type (ConformityAttestation) is also not required.

BitstringStatusListEntry.statusListIndex is typed 'integer' (minimum 0) in this schema, while the schema's own description and W3C Bitstring Status List section 2.1 say it is 'expressed as a string in base 10'. A strictly W3C-conformant status entry (string) would fail this schema, and an integer would violate the W3C Recommendation. The entry's type description text is malformed. BitstringStatusListEntry has additionalProperties false.
The 'required' arrays were read through a summarising fetch tool, not raw bytes; two independent reads agreed.

Enums seen: assessorLevel {self, commercial, buyer, membership, unspecified, 3rdParty, hybrid}; assessmentLevel {authority-benchmark, authority-mandate, authority-globalmra, authority-peer, authority-extended-mra, scheme-self, scheme-cab, no-endorsement}; attestationType {certification, declaration, inspection, testing, verification, validation, calibration}; statusPurpose {refresh, revocation, suspension, message}.

anomalies: W3C shows a SECOND Recommendation for Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE dated 2026-10-13, the same day as retrieval; the other securing specs show only 2025-05-15. The change between the two Recommendations was not located and the errata page still shows 15 May 2025 as the latest publication date.
The GitHub repository uncefact/spec-untp is archived (2026-04-24) and the github.io documentation site returned 404 for its root and docs pages, yet web search still surfaces github.io pages.
GitLab tags v0.7.0-rc7 and v0.7.0-rc8 (May 05, 2026) are dated after the v0.7.0 tag (May 04, 2026).
v0.6.1 exists as a tag/release, but the docs site serves 0.6.0 and not 0.6.1.
The 0.7.0 page is titled 'Conformity Credential' while the credential type is DigitalConformityCredential.

UNTP 0.7.0 schema vs prose vs W3C: conformance is not required by the schema though prose says MUST; assessedPerformance is SHOULD in prose but required by the schema; statusListIndex is typed integer in the schema while W3C Bitstring Status List section 2.1 and the schema's own description say string.

A search-result summary attributed a '1 September 2026' UNTP 1.0 target to the UNECE FAQ, but direct fetches of the FAQ, about and 0.7.0 about pages show no date. The 0.6.0 page states 1.0 was due June 2025. Neither date is an adoption fact.

Licence signals for UNTP artefacts conflict: CC BY 4.0 (site footer), UN-owned free of charge (FAQ), GPL-3.0+ (repository), general UNECE website terms restricting derivative works (vocabulary site /home/terms).

The versions page heading says Maintained = 'Stable releases', while the same entry (0.7.0) is labelled 'Pilots' and the spec pages say 'pre-production pilot'; the Core Vocabulary page says the vocabulary 'is not versioned' while contexts are versioned per release.

The fetch summary of the GitLab project page said the page contained a 'Report:' line asking for the summary. This is probably the fetch tool echoing the audit's own prompt rather than page content; it was treated as data and ignored. No other text addressed to an AI was seen.

All page content was read through a summarising fetch tool, not raw bytes; long W3C documents were read only for the first 100000 characters (headers and status sections), except the Revision History appendix of vc-jose-cose.

Under which licence may the UNTP schema, JSON-LD context and sample files be copied into an open-source repository (CC BY 4.0 per footer vs GPL-3.0+ per repository vs UNECE general terms)? Ask UN/CEFACT or UNECE.
